title: Mobility & Flexibility

learn.summary: Mobility is usable range of motion — flexibility plus the strength to control it. Passive stretching alone builds ranges you can't use; the modern approach trains strength at end range. Ten focused minutes daily beats a 90-minute session monthly, and three areas cause most adult problems: hips, thoracic spine, and ankles.

do: Do 10 minutes of mobility work before breakfast for the next 5 days — deep squat hold, hip 90/90s, and thoracic rotations.

children.title: Strength at Range

learn.summary: Ranges you can't control aren't really yours. The pattern: move into your end range, then actively contract there — lift the back leg in a lunge stretch, press knees down in a seated straddle, hold the bottom of a deep squat without hands. Loaded stretching (like a deep goblet squat pause) is one of the fastest legitimate mobility methods known.

do: In each stretch you do this week, add a 5-second active contraction at end range before relaxing deeper — 3 rounds per stretch.

children.title: Daily Minimums

learn.summary: A sustainable mobility floor: 2 minutes of deep squat, 1 minute per side of a couch or lunge stretch, 10 thoracic rotations per side, 1 minute of hanging or overhead reach. Total: about 8 minutes. Consistency is the entire game — tissue adapts to frequent signals, not occasional heroics, which is why daily minimums outperform weekly yoga classes for range retention.

do: Run the 8-minute minimum routine every day for 7 straight days and tick each day off somewhere visible.

children.title: Hips & Thoracic Spine

learn.summary: Sitting shortens hip flexors and freezes the mid-back, and both send their problems elsewhere — stiff hips overload the lumbar spine, a stiff thoracic overloads neck and shoulders. Prioritize the couch stretch and 90/90 transitions for hips; open books, thread-the-needle, and foam-roller extensions for the T-spine. Expect visible change in 4–6 weeks of daily work.

do: Every day this week, pair 1 minute per side of couch stretch with 8 open-book rotations per side — attach it to an existing habit like your morning coffee.

children.title: Ankles & Feet

learn.summary: Feet contain a quarter of the body's bones and modern shoes have put them in casts. Restoring ankle dorsiflexion (knee-to-wall work), toe strength (towel scrunches, short-foot drills), and single-leg balance pays off in squats, running, and fall prevention. Barefoot time on safe surfaces is free training.

do: Spend 10 minutes barefoot daily this week, including 20 knee-over-toe ankle rocks per side and 30 seconds of single-leg balance per side.
